meet.title: The Homecoming Spread
meet.place: The yearbook office, Glimmer Falls High
meet.text: The yearbook office smells of rubber cement and darkroom chemicals. Chip Merriweather, class president, is redoing the homecoming spread alone at four in the afternoon, because every photo keeps coming out of the developer with gray faces. When you knock he jumps, and a flyer slides out of his binder onto the floor between you: the Glitter Box's Saturday midnight double feature. He goes pale. "That's, um. That's for a civics project. On local... theatre."
meet.art: A cluttered high school yearbook office with photo proofs pinned to corkboard, several faces in the photos drained gray, a preppy boy in a pink oxford frozen beside a desk, a theatre flyer on the floor

choices.label: Hand back the flyer like it is nothing and ask about the photos

success.text: You pass him the flyer without a second look. "Midnight shows are the best ones. So, why are your photos gray?" His shoulders drop an inch, like he's set down something heavy. You fix the spread together until the custodian kicks you out. "Hey," Chip says at the door. "Thanks. For... the help. Can I help you with whatever you're doing? I'd like that."
success.art: A teenager handing a flyer back to a relieved preppy boy in a yearbook office, both bent over photo proofs, late afternoon light through the blinds

failure.text: You hand it back too carefully, and he hears something you didn't mean. His smile snaps back into place, bright and empty. "Student council meeting. Totally forgot. You should come back tomorrow, though. I'm here every day. Every single day."
failure.art: A preppy boy flashing a bright, brittle smile while hurriedly stuffing papers into his binder, a teenager in the doorway of a yearbook office

choices.label: Help him work out why the photos keep turning gray

success.text: Under the red light you see it: the gray always starts at the hair and creeps down, like a dye job in reverse, and only on kids whose parents were in the 1961 PTA. Chip stares. "My mom was PTA secretary." He takes a breath. "Okay. I'm in. Whatever this is, I want to help fix it."
success.art: Two teenagers in a red-lit darkroom examining a dripping photo where a student's hair is turning gray from the roots down

failure.text: A face in the developing tray smiles at you. It is not a face that was in the photograph. Chip drops the tongs. You both stand very still until the red light buzzes out. "Tomorrow," Chip whispers. "In the regular light. Please."
failure.art: A face smiling up from a darkroom developing tray under red light, two teenagers frozen in shock, a pair of tongs falling

choices.label: Pocket the flyer and claim it when his father appears at the door

success.text: "Chipper, the HOA dinner," says a tall man in a golf sweater from the doorway. You tuck the flyer in your own jacket and ask Chip loudly about the homecoming fundraiser. His father nods and leaves. Chip looks at you like you've pulled him out of the quarry lake. "I owe you," he says. "Let me pay it back. I'm with you."
success.art: A tall man in a golf sweater in a yearbook office doorway, a teenager casually tucking a flyer into their jacket, a preppy boy staring at them in quiet gratitude

failure.text: Mr. Merriweather looks at the flyer sticking out of your pocket, then at you, and decides you are a bad influence. You are shown out with great politeness. Through the window, Chip mouths sorry. Come back tomorrow, when his father is at the office.
failure.art: A tall man in a golf sweater politely escorting a teenager out of a school office, a preppy boy behind him mouthing an apology through the window

name: Joey Benally
bio: Joey Benally's family moved from Shiprock, New Mexico, to Glimmer Falls when his mom took a nursing job at County General, and he has hated the fog every day since. He works after school in the garage at Rusty's Junkyard, where he can make anything with an engine run, and he is rebuilding a 1968 pickup to drive home to his grandmother's every summer. He helped Sunny Castellanos build her racing chair out of bicycle parts and stubbornness. Joey is dry, practical and allergic to nonsense; he has a dozen rational explanations for every haunting and is annoyed every time they don't work. His flaw is that he would rather fix everything himself than ask for help, and he trusts machines faster than people.

perk.name: Jump Start
perk.text: Joey gets it running on the second try, every time: reroll one failed daytime roll each day.

meet.title: Under the Pickup
meet.place: Joey's garage, Rusty's Junkyard
meet.text: In the cinderblock garage at the edge of Rusty's, a pair of work boots sticks out from under a 1968 pickup. A radio is playing the farm report. Behind the garage, the car maze creaks and settles like it is breathing, and you could swear the rows were in a different order when you walked in. "If you're here to tell me the junkyard moves at night," says a voice from under the truck, "I've heard it. It's ground settling. Hand me the 9/16."
meet.art: A cinderblock junkyard garage with a 1968 pickup on jacks, work boots sticking out from underneath, a toolbox open on the floor, rows of stacked wrecked cars visible through the door

choices.label: Find the right wrench and keep handing tools without being asked

success.text: 9/16, then the ratchet, then the flashlight before he asks for it. Joey rolls out on the creeper and looks at you for a long second. "Most people hand me a hammer and hope. You can stick around." Coming from Joey, that's a parade.
success.art: A young mechanic rolling out from under a pickup on a creeper and taking a socket wrench from a teenager, a toolbox open between them

failure.text: You hand him a 10mm. He looks at it. He looks at you. He slides back under the truck. "Come back tomorrow when you know a 9/16 from a 10mm. There's a chart on the wall."
failure.art: A young mechanic holding up the wrong wrench with a deadpan stare from under a pickup, a teenager wincing beside a toolbox

choices.label: Help him jump-start the pickup off a junked car

success.text: You hold the cables steady, he turns the key, and the old V8 coughs and roars to life for the first time in years. Joey slaps the hood, almost smiling. "Okay. You're useful and you don't flinch. You can ride shotgun."
success.art: A teenager holding jumper cables between a junked car and a roaring old pickup, a young mechanic leaning out of the driver's seat to slap the hood

failure.text: Sparks jump, and the moment they do, every junked car in the maze honks its horn at once, a long rusty chorus. Joey kills the battery. In the silence, he says flatly, "Ground settling. Come back tomorrow."
failure.art: Rows of rusted wrecked cars in a junkyard with headlights flaring on all at once, a young mechanic and a teenager frozen beside a sparking battery

choices.label: Ask him the right question about the car maze

success.text: "Not whether it moves," you say. "Which way it moves." Joey pauses, then rolls out and draws on the dusty floor with a rag: the rows always shift toward Crystal Street, every night this week. "First person who asked me something useful. Fine. I'm in."
success.art: A young mechanic sketching a map of junkyard rows in the dust on a garage floor with a red rag, a teenager crouched beside him

failure.text: "So is it, like, haunted?" Joey's sigh comes from under the truck, long and weary as a tired engine. "No. Come back tomorrow with a better question." Behind you, the car maze creaks in what sounds a lot like agreement.
failure.art: A teenager standing in a junkyard garage doorway, rows of wrecked cars creaking behind them, work boots sticking out from under a truck

name: Barnaby
role: Junkyard stray and nightmare early-warning system
bio: Barnaby is a tricolor basset hound with ears that drag in puddles, a notch in his left ear from a fight he presumably won, and a nose that can smell a nightmare coming an hour before it arrives. He has lived at Rusty's Junkyard for three winters, sleeping in the back seat of a gutted station wagon; Joey Benally feeds him, Dr. Haddad has stitched him up twice, and nobody has ever successfully given him a bath. He howls at sirens, at the KGLM sign-off and at the Heartstone, which he will not walk past. Barnaby is loyal, brave, deeply food-motivated and stubborn as a parked car; his flaws are sandwich theft and lying down in the exact middle of wherever you are trying to go.

perk.name: Nightmare Nose
perk.text: Barnaby smells a bad dream coming and howls before it lands: +2 on every roll against dream nightmares.

meet.title: Something on the Wind
meet.place: The car maze, Rusty's Junkyard
meet.text: Halfway through Rusty's, something heavy leans against your legs. A basset hound with a red bandana and ears like dish towels is sitting on your foot, looking up at you with enormous sorrowful eyes and also at the sandwich in your hand. Then, all at once, his head whips toward the car maze. His hackles rise, and a growl comes out of him from somewhere deep in the earth. The wind shifts. It smells, faintly, like burnt hair and hairspray.
meet.art: A tricolor basset hound in a faded red bandana sitting on a teenager's foot in a junkyard, hackles raised, staring down a dark row of stacked wrecked cars

choices.label: Crouch down and share your sandwich with him

success.text: You split the sandwich. He takes his half with tremendous dignity, then leans his whole warm weight against you and sighs. When you stand up to leave, he follows. When you stop, he sits on your foot again. Apparently that settles it.
success.art: A teenager crouched in a junkyard sharing a sandwich with a basset hound, the dog leaning contentedly against their side

failure.text: He takes his half. Then he takes your half, and the bag, and vanishes under a rusted tail-finned sedan with a smug thump of his tail. He'll be back tomorrow. He knows where your lunch lives now.
failure.art: A basset hound's tail sticking out from under a rusty tail-finned sedan, an empty sandwich bag nearby, a teenager staring at their empty hands

choices.label: Follow him into the car maze toward the smell

success.text: He leads you nose-down through the maze to a rusted salon hair dryer someone dumped between two wrecks, still warm. Barnaby plants himself between you and it and howls, long and loud, until it goes cold. Then he looks back at you, tail thumping: so, we're a team now.
success.art: A basset hound howling protectively in front of a rusted vintage salon hair dryer between stacked wrecked cars, a teenager behind him

failure.text: The rows shift behind you while you walk. You spend an hour lost with an increasingly nervous basset hound before he finds the way out by smell alone. He sits down at the gate and won't follow you further. Tomorrow, maybe.
failure.art: A teenager and a basset hound lost between towering walls of stacked wrecked cars at dusk, the gaps between rows narrowing
